questions.q: What does the registry style of MDM architecture actually store centrally?
options: A full physical copy of every source system's master data
Nothing — registry style has no central component at all
A complete rewrite of every source system's database schema
Only matching keys and cross-reference links between records in different source systems
questions.explain: Registry style is the lightest touch: source data stays exactly where it is, and the central registry just maps which records across systems refer to the same real-world entity.

questions.q: How does consolidation style differ from coexistence style?
options: Consolidation merges data into a central store one-way for reporting; coexistence syncs bidirectionally so corrections can flow back to sources
They are identical in every respect
Consolidation syncs data back to source systems; coexistence never does
Consolidation requires no central store at all
questions.explain: Consolidation is a one-way mirror good for reporting; coexistence adds bidirectional sync so a correction made centrally can flow back out to the source system.

questions.q: In the centralized (transaction hub) style, where do master data writes happen first?
options: At whichever source system the user happens to be using
There is no concept of a 'first' write in this style
At the central hub, which is the actual system of record; source systems read from it rather than writing their own independent copies
Writes are randomly distributed across all connected systems
questions.explain: Centralized style gives the most control precisely because every create and update happens at the hub first, eliminating independent writes at the source systems.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is a common way MDM programs stall?
options: Using too many architecture styles correctly at once
Jumping straight to a centralized transaction hub before the matching rules underneath it are trusted
Spending too much time matching customer records
Starting with registry style instead of centralized style
questions.explain: The lesson warns that architecture style is a deployment decision layered on top of matching and governance — centralizing before that foundation is solid is called out as a common failure mode.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what is the core structural question every MDM implementation has to answer?
options: How many employees will be hired for the data governance team
Which programming language will be used to build the MDM tool
Where the trusted master data actually lives, and whether source systems keep writing to their own copies or give that up
Which cloud provider offers the lowest storage cost
questions.explain: The lesson frames all four architecture styles as different answers to exactly this one question about where master data lives and who retains independent write access.
